questions.explanation: If you fail, online retakes are limited to two tries in any 24 hours and four tries overall; after that you have to test at a DMV office.

questions.prompt: If you are under 18 and take the knowledge test online, who must supervise, and how many tests may that person supervise in 24 hours?
choices: A friend who is 16.
A supervisor older than 21, who may oversee only two tests in any 24-hour period.
No proctor is required.
A teacher of any age, with no daily limit.
questions.explanation: Testers younger than 18 need a proctor older than 21, and that proctor may supervise only two tests in 24 hours.

questions.prompt: What kind of computer is required for the online knowledge test?
choices: A phone or tablet with a touchscreen is required.
A desktop or laptop computer with a keyboard, mouse, and webcam. You cannot use a touchscreen device like a mobile phone or tablet.
Any smart TV.
A library computer without a webcam.
questions.explanation: The online test has to be taken on a desktop or laptop that has a keyboard, mouse, and webcam—not on a phone or tablet.

questions.prompt: If you fail the drive test, how long must you wait before retaking it?
choices: You may retake it immediately.
The rule is to wait until the next business day.
The rule is to wait 30 days.
The rule is to wait 90 days.
questions.explanation: If you fail the drive test, you have to wait until the next business day to try the drive test again.

questions.prompt: Infants must ride rear-facing until they reach what age?
choices: Six months
One year
Two years of age
Four years
questions.explanation: Infants have to ride facing the rear until they turn two.

questions.prompt: Is there a fee for the DMV vision test?
choices: Yes, $7.
No. The vision screening itself does not have a fee.
It is included only if you fail the knowledge test.
questions.explanation: The vision screening itself does not have a fee.

questions.prompt: If you take the vision test while wearing glasses or contact lenses, what happens?
choices: Nothing is noted on your privilege.
Your privilege will be marked as requiring corrective lenses.
The rule is to retake the test without them.
You cannot be licensed.
questions.explanation: Taking the vision screening in glasses or contacts means your privilege will be marked as requiring corrective lenses.

questions.prompt: Proof of identity and date of birth documents must be what?
choices: A clear photocopy or a phone picture.
Original or certified copies from the issuing agency.
A signed note from a friend.
An expired hospital souvenir certificate.
questions.explanation: Bring originals or certified copies from the agency that issued the document, not ordinary photocopies.

questions.prompt: Is a hospital-issued birth certificate or a baptismal record acceptable as proof of date of birth?
choices: Yes, both are preferred.
No. A U.S. government-issued birth certificate is acceptable, but hospital-issued birth certificates and baptismal records are not.
Only baptismal records are accepted.
Yes, if notarized by a teacher.
questions.explanation: The most common forms of proof include a U.S. government-issued birth certificate. A hospital-issued birth certificate or a baptismal record will not be accepted.

questions.prompt: When applying for a driving privilege, how many documents must you present to prove your current residence address?
choices: None, a verbal statement is always enough on its own.
One document, such as business, school, or government mail that shows your first and last name. Personal letters and forwarded mail do not count.
Five utility bills from different years.
A photo of your front door.
questions.explanation: One document is enough to prove a standard (non-REAL ID) residence address. Mail from a business, school, or government office that shows your first and last name is common. Personal letters and forwarded mail do not count.

questions.prompt: Can a person who lives at the same address certify your address?
choices: No one else may help.
Yes, if that person comes with you and shows their own address proof, such as a license or ID card.
Yes, by a phone call, without coming in.
Only a landlord letter sent later by email.
questions.explanation: Common proof includes a housemate can confirm your address in person by coming with you and showing their own license or ID as proof.
